study_identification_part.si4_title: Mapping cerebellar anatomical heterogeneity in mental and neurological illnesses

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To map the normative development and aging of the cerebellum across the lifespan using brain scans of >54,000 participants, and to reveal heterogeneity in cerebellar anatomy within five clinical illnesses (autism spectrum disorder, mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer disease, bipolar disorder, and schizophrenia) using voxel-wise precision normative models.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group-based nonparametric tests: Two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests with rank biserial correlation (r) to compare z scores between clinical groups and individuals without diagnosis; Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons (across ROIs/voxels, number of clinical groups, and directions); Atlas-based case-control analyses: Mann-Whitney U tests comparing percentage of extreme deviations between clinical groups and controls across three atlases (28 anatomical lobules, 10 task-based regions, 17 resting-state connectivity regions); Correlation analyses: Spearman correlation between percentage of extreme deviations and cognitive/symptom scores (IQ scores: FIQ, VIQ, PIQ; ADOS for ASD; PANSS for SZ); Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons (number of tests, ROIs, and directions); only correlations with corrected P < 0.05 reported as significant
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Individuals with ASD and MCI exhibited increased positive and negative extreme deviations in cerebellar anatomy, while those with SZ and AD showed predominantly negative deviations; extreme deviations were associated with cognitive scores in ASD and SZ.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study developed approximately 143,000 normative models of cerebellar lobules and voxels across the lifespan using >54,000 individuals. Group-level analyses revealed: (1) SZ showed significant negative effect sizes indicating lower cerebellar volumes, particularly in posterior regions; (2) AD and MCI exhibited negative deviations in lobular volumes and right V/crus I regions; (3) ASD showed negative deviations in anterior regions for lobular volumes and small negative effects in posterior regions for voxel-wise maps; (4) BD showed no significant effects after multiple comparison correction. Individual-level heterogeneity was substantial: even within the same diagnostic group, only a marginal percentage showed extreme deviations in the same regions, though some posterior lobules showed increased deviations across multiple disorders. Atlas-based analyses revealed small to medium effects across all three atlases (anatomical, task-based, resting-state). For ASD, medium effects in negative deviations were seen in regions related to action observation/divided attention (task-based) and dorsal attention network (resting-state). Cognitive associations: In ASD, regions in right IV-VI (anatomical) and somatomotor B network (resting-state) showed positive correlations between percentage of extreme positive deviations and estimated PIQ that survived multiple comparisons. In SZ, weak positive correlations were found between percentage of extreme positive deviations and estimated intelligence scores across three atlases, and vice versa for negative deviations. ADOS scores for ASD and PANSS scores for SZ did not show significant associations after correction.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Lack of coherent behavioral, cognitive, genetic, phenotypic, and medical history information across datasets; relatively low coverage of lifespan models in very young age and 30-40 years age range; primarily represents western/European populations limiting generalizability; incomplete medication information for TOP study; inferior cerebellar regions may have poorer model fits due to imaging challenges; cerebellar topography shows substantial individual differences not perfectly aligned with average atlases; IQ estimates based on wide range of tests across groups are not accurate reflections of intelligence; cross-sectional data limits examination of drug/treatment effects
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: First, we lack coherent and detailed behavioral, cognitive, genetic, phenotypic, and medical history information for both individuals without diagnosis and clinical samples ... the coverages of lifespan normative models in the very young age and in the age range of 30-40 years were relatively low ... Due to limited availability regarding ethnicity information, this paper represents primarily western populations, in particular, European groups, which limits its generalizability ... the local thematically organized psychosis (TOP) study has incomplete information regarding medication status and duration ... Because of its location in the posterior fossa, its intricate arrangement, and motions artifacts, the cerebellum has posed challenges in imaging studies, and therefore inferior regions of the cerebellum may result in poorer model fits ... The cerebellar topography shows substantial individual differences and therefore does not perfectly align with existing 'average' atlases ... the IQ estimates used here are based on a wide range of tests used across groups. The IQ measures used here are mere estimates of intelligence and not an accurate reflection of intelligence ... This paper focuses on large-baseline cross-sectional data, which limits the examination of the effects of drugs or treatment

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study integrated voxel-wise normative models with multiple cerebellar atlases (anatomical, task-based functional, resting-state connectivity) to enhance functional interpretation of deviations. Supplementary sensitivity analyses included: (1) sex-, age-, and scanning-site-matched control comparisons; (2) ethnicity-matched analyses for European subgroups in SZ and BD; (3) subgroup analyses within ASD (Asperger's Syndrome vs Autism based on DSM-IV); (4) exploratory correlations between total antipsychotic medication load and deviations in SZ (not significant after correction). The models are made publicly available via PCNportal for future research.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This is one of the largest multi-site investigations of cerebellar development and aging with both voxel-wise and lobular spatial precision. The study year is 2024 (published online August 22, 2024) but the first author is Kim, hence Study ID should be Kim2024. The normative models cover approximately 143,000 voxels and 28 lobular regions from 132 scanning sites. Initial dataset included 58,709 individuals without diagnosis and 3,764 clinical individuals before QC exclusions. Final analyzed sample: 54,102 healthy controls (27,117 training, 26,985 testing) and 1,757 clinical participants. The study demonstrates substantial within-disorder heterogeneity using individual-level normative probability maps.
